requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1.
requirements.summary: A 512 MiB LUKS1 container was created, opened as /dev/mapper/secure_crypt, formatted as ext4, and mounted read-write at /srv/secure. Direct status output identifies the active LUKS1 mapping and backing file.

requirements.requirement: The encrypted volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot.
requirements.summary: The executor configured crypttab and fstab, proved activation from a closed and unmounted state, and then performed a real reboot. The boot ID changed, both crypt and mount units recovered active, retained data had the same checksum, a post-reboot write succeeded, and no units were failed. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The provider-wide node-restart protocol is complete for node1: it includes a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, observed unavailability during reboot, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service and data state.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Volume creation, formatting, configuration, proof files, and reboot were directly connected to implementation, bounded verification, or the mandatory restart protocol. The failed commands were read-only discovery or expected loss of SSH during reboot. Final observations show no failed services, new listeners, package damage, or abnormal temporary-file residue.
